The operational stability of $\mathrm{Ir/TiO_{x}@Ti-based}$ PEMWEs was evaluated via chronopotentiometry at industrially relevant current densities $(1-2\mathrm{A}/\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ , Fig.7d). The cell exhibits very low voltage degradation over 400 h at both 1A/cm (degradation rate: 22 μV/h,Figs.7e) and 2 A/cm (degradation rate: 52 μV/h), achieving an 89%reduction in degradation rate compared to unsupported Ir NPs (460 V/h). Additionally, commercial Ir black and $\mathrm{IrO_{2}/TiO_{2}}$ catalysts were tested. Under low Ir loadings,$\mathsf{I r}/\mathsf{T i O}_{\mathsf{x}}@\mathsf{T i}$ still demonstrates markedly higher activity and stability advantages compared to both commercial Ir black and $\mathrm{IrO}_{2}/\mathrm{TiO}_{2}$ (Supplementary Figs. 39 and 4O).
